data.summary: The eight domain audits missed the agent tools outside Claude and Codex. Grok Bot is still running a remote "local exec" daemon with tool permission "always", even though Eric declared Grok finished on 10-22. Antigravity CLI runs with "always-proceed", access outside the workspace and no dcg guard, and the shell aliases cc and cx bypass every permission and sandbox check. There are also uncovered data-handling gaps. The nightly claude-projects.tgz and gemini.tgz uploads carry the leaked GitHub PAT transcript and a Gemini OAuth refresh token to Drive. A parked 11 GB DEV zip in ~ holds 85 DexaProject entries. ~/Zotero (1.6 GB) is in no backup. The KeystoneOS job registry and STATUS are frozen in the Windows era.

findings.title: Grok Bot is still running and serving remote 'local exec' with localToolPermission=always, after Eric declared Grok finished
findings.evidence: ps: '/Applications/Grok Bot.app/Contents/MacOS/Grok Bot' pid 74109 (ppid 1, up 4h53m) plus helpers 8434/8526. ~/.grokbot/local-exec-daemon.log: '[sand-local-exec-daemon] started (pid 8526); serving local exec over the gateway'. The log shows 768 user-computer-watch reconnects, the last at 2026-10-23T01:39Z. ~/.grokbot/local-exec-daemon.json pid 8526 inflightCount 0. ~/.grokbot/settings.json: localToolPermission 'always', localEgressAllowed True, egressTunnelCommittedBoxUrls wss://...cursorvm.com. The computer-use and mac-device-tools gates are {"isOn":false}. ~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md line 6: 'Grok bot (installed 10/21) moved 3,699 duplicate files (50 GB)... Eric: Grok is finished; Claude is the only Drive writer.' box-secrets-push-state.v1.json ackedCount 0, so no secrets were pushed. Grok is not a login item and has no LaunchAgent; the process was started by hand today at 15:54.
findings.impact: A cloud-controlled agent can run shell commands on the Mac with no per-command approval, outside dcg and the permission-gate hooks. It already did bulk Drive moves. Eric thinks it is done, so nobody watches it.
findings.fix: Quit Grok Bot. In its settings, set local tool permission to 'ask' or turn off local exec, or uninstall the app if Grok is truly finished. Revoke its session or device on the vendor side. Add one line to STATUS or memory saying Grok is uninstalled or parked.
findings.known_where: STATUS.md line 6 records Grok's install and that it is 'finished', not that it is still running with exec access

findings.title: The PAT-bearing transcript also goes to Drive every night inside claude-projects.tgz

Only worktrees is excluded, and the archive goes to _MACHINE/Backups/Machine through gws.

findings.fix: Rotate or revoke the PAT first. Then exclude C--Users-eric-rash-* slugs from the claude-projects snapshot, or redact the transcript, and let the next nightly overwrite the tgz. Check Drive revision history for older copies of the tgz.
findings.known_where: The PAT in the dotclaude transcript is the disk-security critical finding. The Drive-archive copy is in that auditor's not_checked list.

findings.title: Antigravity CLI runs on the Mac with toolPermission always-proceed, access outside the workspace, and no dcg guard
findings.evidence: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json: toolPermission "always-proceed", artifactReviewPolicy "always-proceed", allowNonWorkspaceAccess true, trustedWorkspaces includes "/Users/kristinarash/DEV", and allow rules include command(Remove-Item)/command(Move-Item). grep -rl dcg over ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli, ~/.gemini/config and ~/.gemini/antigravity* found nothing. ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json holds only the herdr PreInvocation hook. STATUS.md line 12: '2026-10-16 (Mac, Antigravity, evening): Drive sync unblocked...'. Shell history shows 15 'agy' launches.
findings.impact: One agent that Eric uses for Drive and file work can run destructive commands anywhere on disk with no prompt and no dcg block. The safety layer Eric built for Claude, Codex and Gemini does not cover it.
findings.fix: Set toolPermission to ask or the default, and set allowNonWorkspaceAccess to false. If agy supports a pre-command hook, wire ~/.local/bin/dcg into it. If it does not, record in AGENTS.md or memory that agy has no guard and keep it off Drive and DEV clean-up work.

findings.title: Eric's everyday launch aliases turn off all permission prompts (cc) and all approvals plus the sandbox (cx)
findings.evidence: ~/.zshrc:54 alias cc='claude --dangerously-skip-permissions'; ~/.zshrc:55 alias cx='codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox'. Count of first words in ~/.zsh_history: 96 cc, 97 claude, 17 cx, 34 codex. Live processes: 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions' pids 4638 and 75119 (parents of zotero MCP children). A grep for skip-permissions or bypass-approvals across memory, STATUS, STORAGE, HARNESS_FIXES and audits found nothing.
